counterevidence_search.method: Checked cross-references from the dated governing edition and inspected its linked official errata page. Targeted public searches checked for a contrary focus rule in the W3C errata and discussion locations.
counterevidence_search.result: The linked errata page was a placeholder. No applicable contrary controlling text surfaced. Apparent conflict with general focus preservation resolves at the specific callee declaration rule.

historical_boundary.disposition: Existing rejected revision preserved. This review assesses revision 2 only.

independent_control_passages.section: External initial named template invocation has a separate entry focus.
Restoration, absent focus expression errors and detailed instruction precedence.
A supplied parameter value takes precedence over a nonmandatory default.
Caller-side parameter value calculation uses the parent instruction focus.
Named call resolution and the irrelevance of match, mode and priority to the named invocation.
Permitted use values, placement, default, absent/as static rule and typing boundaries.
Omitted and explicit absent branches, rule-selection separation and required-item errors.

limitations: Only the 8 June 2017 XSLT 3.0 Recommendation and the two stated valid named-call branches were assessed.

The focus is the initial evaluation context of the callee constructor and callee parameter evaluation. Supplied caller-side argument expressions, unused defaults, later focus changes within instructions, and focus-dependent evaluation errors have separate rules.
The challenge directly evaluated the normative rules. No stylesheet processor was run and no implementation behavior was measured.
Independent Codex execution verified the same governing source. The execution does not supply a second normative authority.

paper_challenge.result: At the start of the callee constructor the focus is item right, position 3, size 4. The call does not create a singleton focus.
paper_challenge.setup: The caller is on item right, at position 3 of a four-item sequence, and calls a visible named template without a context declaration.

paper_challenge.result: All three focus components are absent within the constructor and callee parameter evaluation. Incoming focus presence does not invalidate the call.
paper_challenge.setup: The same visible template has a first-child xsl:context-item use=absent with no as attribute, a context-independent default parameter, and a context-independent body.

paper_challenge.result: The caller-side expression uses the call instruction focus. The resulting value is an ordinary supplied argument. Callee parameter-default evaluation has the absent focus when used.
paper_challenge.setup: For that absent-focus callee, the caller also supplies a parameter using xsl:with-param selecting the caller context item.

paper_challenge.result: The match attribute does not choose the target or set its focus in this invocation. Pattern-driven dispatch remains a separate path.
paper_challenge.setup: The named callee also declares a match pattern, and the instruction still resolves it by name.

paper_challenge.result: The first is XTSE3088 and excluded by validity. Explicit optional and required declarations have separate rules. The missing required context is XTTE3090, outside the claim conditions.
paper_challenge.setup: Try a declaration with use=absent plus as, an explicit optional declaration, or a required declaration with missing incoming focus.

paper_challenge.result: The focus components have no values. This does not describe the body result. A context-dependent expression can encounter XPDY0002 under the detailed absent-focus rules.
paper_challenge.setup: Compare the initial callee focus in the absent branch to a body expression that returns an empty sequence.
